title: Properties Graph
summary: Given a 2D integer array properties with dimensions n x m and an integer k, define a function intersect(a, b) that counts the number of distinct integers common to both arrays a and b.
statement: Given a 2D integer array properties with dimensions n x m and an integer k, define a function intersect(a, b) that counts the number of distinct integers common to both arrays a and b. Construct an undirected graph where each index i represents properties[i]. An edge exists between node i and node j if intersect(properties[i], properties[j]) is at least k, with i and j ranging from 0 to n-1 and i not equal to j. Return the count of connected components in this graph.
constraints: properties is a nonempty list of integer lists and k is positive.
Two nodes are adjacent when their property lists share at least k distinct values.
Return the number of connected components in the resulting undirected graph.
hints: Only distinct property values matter, and connected components can be merged as qualifying pairs are found.
Convert every row to a set, compare all node pairs, and union roots when intersection size reaches k.
Use path compression in find; after all pair checks, count distinct roots.
Union operations create exactly the transitive closure of qualifying graph edges, so remaining roots equal graph components.
editorial: Union operations create exactly the transitive closure of qualifying graph edges, so remaining roots equal graph components.

tests.explanation: The shared-value edges form three connected components.
Duplicates do not count twice, so the two nodes share only one distinct value and remain separate.
